questions.question: Which source kinds are admissible, and what is the paywall/login rule?
questions.explanation: The mission lens says 'Anthropic official best practice'. The line needs drawing: Anthropic docs (docs.claude.com), Anthropic engineering blog and cookbook, Claude Code release notes and repo, conference talks by Anthropic staff, and then the wider world — community posts, third-party writeups. And a source behind a login or paywall needs a decided outcome before research hits one.
options: Anthropic-published only (docs, engineering blog, cookbook, official repos, release notes); paywalled/login sources excluded
Anthropic-published primary, plus talks and interviews given by Anthropic staff; paywalled sources cited but marked unresolved
Anthropic-published preferred, reputable secondary admitted when no primary source exists for a topic, recorded as secondary in the register
questions.recommendation: Anthropic-published primary plus staff talks — several concept topics (abandoning failed runs, dynamic workflows) live in talks and long-form posts rather than docs pages.

questions.question: What are the numbers: recency cutoff, per-topic source budget, and the time-box that defines a stalled search?
questions.explanation: The primer requires each constraint to carry a number or a test. Claude Code guidance moves fast; old advice about agents is often inverted by newer models. A per-topic budget and time-box define when research stops and the gap is recorded in the unresolved field (edge E1).
options: Cutoff: nothing older than 2024; budget: 3-7 sources per topic; stalled after 2 focused search passes with no admissible source
Cutoff: nothing older than mid-2023 (Claude Code era only for tooling topics, looser for concepts); budget: up to 5 sources; stalled after 1 pass
No hard cutoff, but every source older than 12 months carries a note that it predates the current model generation; budget and time-box as the run's orchestrator sets them
questions.recommendation: Option 1 — hard, checkable numbers; 2024+ covers the whole public life of Claude Code and the agent-orchestration guidance wave.
